defects.source: PR #391 independent review (Codex P1, CodeRabbit Major) on 2026-08-30. The first correction for the API-only code-write ingress gap asserted prevention using a denylist of committer logins, emails and names. The Contents API and Git Data API let a caller supply any author and committer identity, so an API-only write evaded the denylist and could still reach hosted preflight success; the check also read only the tip, so a clone-authored tip concealed an API-written ancestor. The policy is read by the governance controller from the trusted default branch, so a candidate cannot widen its own allowlist or move its own attestation floor. Only the committer login is trusted for signer identity because a verified signature binds the committer email to the key owner; the author field carries no such binding. Commits reachable from the declared attested_from_commit floor predate the authority and are exempt, and three-dot comparison excludes only ancestors of that floor, so the exemption cannot be steered onto a later commit. defects.source: Issue #403 governed ChatGPT/trusted-connector code-write ingress, 2026-08-31
defects.guard_boundary: Connector code-write authorization and exact-head candidate admission
defects.guard: docs/CODE_WRITE_POLICY.json connector_write_ingress is the only grant that can authorize a non-clone code write, and it is read by the governance controller from the trusted default branch so a candidate cannot grant itself ingress. hunter_connector_write_ingress rejects, fail-closed, a disabled or unbound grant, an unauthorized writer, a writer without the granted capability, a non-branch or protected-branch target (so a direct main write is unrepresentable), a branch whose name does not bind the one declared governing Issue, a base ref other than the authorized base, a base commit that is not the exact observed base tip, and any changed path that is prohibited or outside the granted scope -- including the hooks, workflows, scripts, and policy files that bind the ingress itself. It shares one path-scope semantic with the workflow state gate rather than defining a second one, and admission re-uses the authorizer's own check_scope. The base tip is never caller-supplied: it is resolved from trusted repository state at authorization time and re-checked immediately before the write is applied, so a stale caller cannot certify its own staleness and an authorization cannot be applied after the base advances. Because a verified signature from an allowlisted account proves only who wrote a commit and never that the write crossed the authorizer, an authorized decision mints a canonical claim set whose authorization_id is a SHA-256 over exactly those claims; the writer commits it to the candidate head, and hunter_governance_review_v2 re-derives every claim from trusted repository and pull-request evidence -- branch, base, fork point, governing Issue derived from the branch itself, committer of every attested commit, and the trusted changed-file list re-scoped against the grant. A connector-namespace branch without a receipt, a receipt outside the namespace, a receipt understating the changed files, or one minted for another branch, Issue, or fork point all fail admission however green the hosted statuses are. The connector authenticates as an account that is also a clone-capable signer, so committer login cannot separate the channels and identity disjointness would only make the grant unbindable; the channels are separated by evidence instead: the grant may not declare pre-push equivalence, an active grant must declare that trusted hosted exact-head proof is required for all candidates or the loader and guard refuse it, and while the grant is active a verified signature alone admits nothing -- every code-changing range additionally requires the trusted hosted exact-head canonical preflight status for that exact head and PR, in addition to the existing exact-head branch preflight. families.invariant: A new issuer instance must never fail or terminally mutate active work owned by another live instance: an active CLAIMED/DISPATCHED execution carries the exact owner identity and a renewable lease, expired ownership may be recovered fail-closed, and authorization replay identity is never released.

applicability.rationale: The execution ledger and the issuer composition root are where one instance can mistake another live instance's active execution for its own leftover work; the owner/lease columns, startup recovery and the second-instance overlap live there.

prevention.mechanism: Owner- and lease-aware execution ledger: every active row carries the exact owning issuer instance id and a renewable lease, and startup recovery fails closed only incomplete rows whose lease has lapsed, never a row under a valid foreign lease. complete/fail/record_dispatch require the exact owning instance, the owning instance renews each still-running execution's lease, and replay identity stays permanently claimed so lease expiry never permits a reclaim or re-execution.

families.title: accepted-execution-shutdown-drain-safety
families.invariant: Once /issue-agent/authorize has accepted and durably dispatched work, process shutdown must not silently abandon the provider worker: accepted execution workers are tracked and gracefully drained to a terminal outcome, and a drain timeout must not fabricate FAILED for work still genuinely running.

applicability.rationale: The trusted issuer HTTP edge and its background execution workers are where accepted work can be silently abandoned at shutdown or falsely failed when a drain timeout expires while the provider still runs.

prevention.mechanism: Accepted execution workers are non-daemon and registered before start, unregister themselves on completion, and are joined by an idempotent IssuerServer.shutdown() snapshot taken outside the registry lock; a drain timeout expires without ever writing a FAILED row, leaving the live row owned by the genuine owner while its provider still runs.

families.title: merge-readiness-without-current-head-review-authority
families.invariant: The final Merge Readiness controller must itself fail closed unless a complete exact-head review exists at the current PR head and verifies against trusted PR evidence -- a missing, stale, incomplete, or still-contested review is a hard merge blocker, never a warning. The review authority is an ordered reviewer pool declared by the trusted default branch, and that declaration is what names its members: authority-eligible reviewers are attempted in strict priority order, a reviewer the pool marks triage-only (authority_eligible false) is never review authority however substantive its output, and the deterministic hostile-review guard the pool declares as its last_resort is the last resort. Any reviewer below the primary is admissible only when it records, in machine-checkable fields (reviewer_attempts), that every higher-priority authority-eligible reviewer was actually attempted and exhausted with a recorded reason and recorded budgets within the bounded timeout policy -- acknowledgement and review are separately budgeted, so an attempt proves exhaustion only when both recorded budgets are within policy and the review budget was actually spent; the guard is admissible only when the whole enabled pool is exhausted AND it records why the pool reviewers could not review and that Governance, trusted Preflight, a zero unresolved-thread count, and complete structured evidence were all green at review time. A review that silently skips an enabled reviewer while it is available, a guard review whose exhaustion cannot be proven (missing, skipped, duplicated, malformed, unknown-agent, or out-of-bounds attempts), a review whose recorded exact head differs from the candidate head, or a new commit after the review all invalidate the review and force reviewer selection to restart. A resolved review finding counts as satisfied only when its structured evidence names the exact-head correction commit and a regression test committed in the change set. The pool declaration must also be executable by the collector that consumes it: a reviewer may not be enabled with a trigger method the trusted collector cannot actually perform, because ordered collection fails closed -- an unperformable trigger does not skip its own reviewer, it aborts the walk before every lower-priority reviewer behind it is attempted -- and the budgets recorded on an attempt must be exactly the budgets the pool declares for that reviewer, so a retired budget field can never remain the one the collector or the receipt verifier reads. No other controller's earlier word, and no resolved review thread without that evidence, can stand in for this prerequisite; failover is a deterministic machine decision, never a human-noticed skip.

applicability.rationale: The final merge gate and the single shared review-verification implementation are where the workflow-ordering defect lives: Merge Readiness could go green through governance or check status alone, or a resolved thread could satisfy readiness without machine-verified structured evidence. A recurrence here means the fail-closed prerequisite was weakened at the boundary that is supposed to own it. The fallback authority rule lives here too because a single primary review authority that can be rate-limited or unavailable is itself a workflow freeze waiting to happen: readiness must stay fail-closed without turning Codex availability into a single point of failure. The trusted reviewer collector workflow and implementation are part of the same boundary because they prove ordered reviewer invocation and exhaustion; losing their trigger permission or sequencing can silently disable failover and recreate a single-reviewer freeze.

prevention.mechanism: Review authority is bound to the exact current HEAD, never an ancestor, including artifact-only and empty descendants. Authenticated submitted reviewer evidence must match the structured authority. Bare native Codex issue comments are not authority in the shared verifier; only submitted review objects or structured acknowledgements are admissible there. Lower-priority and Guard reviews require trusted PR-bound exhaustion results emitted by each configured higher-priority reviewer, with matching HEAD, priority, timeout, trigger, parser and retry policy, and API-backed reviewers must re-derive their persisted structured trigger/result evidence rather than trusting a reused invocation marker or a github-actions acknowledgement alone. Collector receipt verification is bound to the run's own immutable trusted default-branch revision and artifact, and that revision must remain on trusted default-branch history rather than being rebound to today's moving default-branch tip. Candidate prose and invocation references alone are not authority. Unconfigured evidence channels fail closed. Governance admission and Merge Readiness share this verifier. A reviewer enabled in the ordered pool must declare a trigger method the collector implements: the Defect Prevention guard calls the collector's own dispatch registry (hunter_reviewer_collector.unsupported_pool_triggers) at the push boundary rather than restating it, so the guard and the implementation cannot drift. A workflow-dispatched reviewer is bound to the trusted default branch and to a per-invocation correlation identity the run renders as its run name, and its result is admissible only from that run's immutable, digest-verified artifact, parsed as an exact-head, claims-bound, internally consistent hunter.local-review.v1 document; anything else is unavailability, never a verdict. A triage-only reviewer is verified positionally so a skipped reviewer is still caught, but never appears in reviewer_attempts, which the shared authority verifier admits only for authority-eligible reviewers.

families.title: preflight-not-enforced-before-ledger-claim-on-every-execution-entry-point
families.invariant: A governed acceptance may not claim the execution ledger before the canonical Source Handling validation has succeeded for the exact authorization, and that ordering must hold on every execution entry point. The service API and the deployed issuer HTTP path are the same governed operation: if the deployed path claims the ledger and dispatches while skipping the preflight the service path runs, a failed or denied acceptance is claimed as if it were authorized. Preflight failure therefore creates no ledger row, the acceptance remains earlier-state replayable once the authority is fixed, and a second entry point that bypasses the seam is itself the defect.

applicability.rationale: The execution ledger and the deployed issuer HTTP edge are the two entry points that can claim an acceptance before Source Handling validation; any future execution surface that skips the shared preparation seam reopens the retry-deadlock defect.

prevention.mechanism: Both entry points resolve Source Handling authority in a single shared preparation seam before any ledger claim: scripts/hunter_issue_agent_issuer.py::prepare_authorization (used by execute_authorization and by the /issue-agent/authorize HTTP path) mirrors src/hunter/automation/issue_agent_execution.py::execute, so the service API and the deployed issuer path run the identical preflight-before-claim ordering. A preflight failure leaves no ledger row and allows the acceptance to be retried once the authority is fixed; a restrictive successor or denied scope is never claimed or dispatched.

families.title: exhausted-exact-head-review-cycle-has-no-review-after-remediation-transition
families.invariant: Remediating the authenticated blocking findings of an exact-head review cycle must be able to start exactly one new review generation for that same exact head and claims, and must never be able to start more than that. The permission to start it is a remediation generation: a deterministic identity derived from trusted GitHub state only -- the exact head, the claims digest, and the set of resolved blocking review threads, where a thread counts as a blocking finding only when an authenticated reviewer app that is neither Hunter's own automation nor the pull-request author opened it. Candidate prose, a candidate-authored thread the candidate then resolves, a dispatch input, a re-run, or a remembered result may never advance it: the trusted default-branch orchestrator derives the generation and the trusted collector re-derives it independently and fails closed on disagreement. The generation must be part of every identity that decides whether a reviewer is invoked again -- the collector run name, the reviewer invocation key, the reviewer trigger body, and the collector receipt -- so that an advanced generation buys exactly one invocation per reviewer and an unchanged generation buys none, and so that exhaustion recorded under a superseded generation is refused rather than replayed to justify a lower-priority authority. The transition is bounded on every side: it requires a material change of generation, it requires the previous generation's collector to be finished and no collector to already exist for this one, and one exact head may spend only a bounded number of generations before the candidate stays pending. Everything the previous boundary owned is unchanged by it: exact-head and claims binding, authenticated reviewer identity, fail-closed pending semantics, zero unresolved review threads, and human merge approval.

applicability.rationale: The orchestrator decides whether a reviewer is invoked again for an immutable head, the collector owns the invocation identity that decision is spent against, and the reconcile workflow is the only trusted surface that runs the orchestrator. A regression in any of them restores the terminal state PR #473 exposed, where a fully remediated candidate can never obtain review authority again.

prevention.mechanism: scripts/hunter_defect_prevention_preflight.py::validate_review_after_remediation_boundary runs inside the Defect Prevention Guard at the push boundary and in the hosted preflight. It checks the invariant semantically against the live implementation rather than by wording: that the remediation generation separates reviewer invocation identities and collector run names while the base generation reproduces the pre-remediation identity exactly; that the generation survives a round trip through both the native and API reviewer triggers and that a substituted generation does not verify; that the generation identity binds exact head, claims digest and resolved thread set and is a deterministic function of that evidence; that the budget is a positive bound and an unchanged generation is never admissible; and that the reviewer collector workflow both accepts the generation input and forwards it to the collector, which re-derives it from trusted review-thread state.

families.title: external-reviewer-availability-cannot-deadlock-merge-authority
families.invariant: External LLM reviewers are optional defense-in-depth, never a mandatory availability dependency for push, candidate admission, governance success, or merge readiness. Provider absence, quota exhaustion, rate limits, timeouts, or stale/missing optional review evidence cannot block an otherwise deterministically verified exact head. Authenticated blocking findings that do exist remain fail-closed until resolved through canonical findings, review threads, or CHANGES_REQUESTED. Human approval remains required for merge.

applicability.rationale: These surfaces can accidentally turn an optional external reviewer into a mandatory liveness dependency and recreate the multi-PR deadlock observed from PR #471 through PR #485.

prevention.mechanism: CODE_WRITE_POLICY declares deterministic governance as merge authority; Defect Prevention rejects mandatory external-review authority; merge readiness ignores reviewer availability while preserving canonical finding blockers; pre-push never blocks on optional review freshness.

families.title: readiness-probe-must-exercise-real-execution-boundary

applicability.rationale: These surfaces select or admit the Issue Agent execution backend and can diverge between readiness and real execution.

prevention.mechanism: Railway IssuerServer defaults execution admission to disabled and the authorization handler returns 503 before slot acquisition, ledger claim, handoff compilation, dispatch, or provider invocation. Only explicit test harnesses can exercise the retired legacy path.

families.title: candidate-code-must-not-execute-with-publication-credentials
families.invariant: Candidate-controlled hooks, scripts, tests, plugins, or other executable repository content never execute inside a boundary that holds candidate-publication write/signing credentials.

applicability.rationale: These surfaces can validate or publish Issue Agent candidate output and therefore define the candidate-code/publication-credential privilege boundary.

prevention.mechanism: The replacement-executor boundary accepts provider output only as a closed-schema hostile file-data result bound to the signed authorization, exact base, derived branch and canonical TaskScope. Rehearsal rejects every publication credential, publisher environments reject model/provider authority, and a validation receipt binds the exact result digest plus validation-definition identity before a separate publisher may consume it. families.title: candidate-must-pass-canonical-preflight-before-pr-publication
families.invariant: A candidate may be pushed only through the repository pre-push safety boundary; the full canonical pytest proof runs exactly once in the hosted exact-HEAD Pre-PR stage, and a Draft PR may be opened only after that hosted proof succeeds. Focused tests are diagnostic evidence and never substitute for the hosted canonical proof.

families.title: tracked-governance-asset-not-loadable-at-its-path
families.invariant: Every tracked governance asset resolves to a path its declared consumer can actually load, and no tracked path carries characters that the consumer's own path grammar rejects. A tracked asset its consumer cannot load contributes no enforcement, and its absence must be a machine-detected condition rather than a silent one.

applicability.rationale: These are the surfaces that hold tracked enforcement assets. Loadability is decided by the consumer's path grammar, not by the repository, so an asset stored anywhere else -- including a path that merely resembles a canonical one -- is inert. Note that a prefix match on '.github/workflows/' does not match a directory whose name differs by an invisible character, which is how the recorded instance escaped selection.

prevention.mechanism: Recorded finding only. A correcting contribution must derive each tracked asset's loadability from the consumer's own path grammar over the tracked path set and reject any asset whose stored path cannot be loaded, before this family can advance. The recorded instance must not be remediated by renaming the asset into a loadable path, because doing so would activate the superseded action major, floating third-party action tag, and repository secret exposure it declares.

families.title: transient-retry-budget-not-derived-from-operation-timeout
families.invariant: A retry budget over a long-running operation is derived from that operation's own timeout rather than stated independently, so exhausting the budget while the operation still has time left is not reachable. A transient upstream refusal is retried only within a budget the operation timeout affords, and budget exhaustion is a distinguishable outcome from terminal refusal.

applicability.rationale: These surfaces carry the webhook dispatch transport, its attempt and backoff constants, and the workflow that supplies the operation timeout the budget must be reconciled against.

prevention.mechanism: Recorded finding only. A correcting contribution must derive the attempt count and backoff ceiling from the operation timeout declared for the same dispatch, and must classify retry-budget exhaustion as a state distinct from terminal refusal, before this family can advance.

families.title: external-precondition-asserted-inside-deterministic-test-lane
families.invariant: The deterministic validation lane asserts only on repository-owned state. A precondition owned outside the repository -- an Issue body, a remote API response, a live network endpoint -- is validated on the runtime path that actually consumes it and reported as its own attributable signal, never as a deterministic-lane assertion whose failure is indistinguishable from a defect in the change under test.

applicability.rationale: These surfaces define the deterministic lane and the owner-authored Issue-body contract that was observed being asserted from inside it, so they are where lane purity is decided and where the external precondition is defined.

prevention.mechanism: Recorded finding only. A correcting contribution must keep the deterministic lane hermetic -- classifying any test whose truth depends on Issue bodies, remote API state, or a live endpoint as integration, and giving integration failures an attributable signal distinct from deterministic failures -- before this family can advance. The owner-authored task-scope contract itself must not be relaxed; the defect is the lane that asserts it, not the contract.

families.title: workflow-environment-dependency-not-provisioned
families.invariant: Every import reachable from a required workflow's entrypoint is satisfied by that workflow's own provisioning step before the entrypoint runs, and provisioning failure is surfaced as a provisioning failure. A declared runtime dependency that is not importable in the environment that needs it is a provisioning defect, not a runtime import error.

applicability.rationale: Workflow definitions, declared project dependencies, reachable persistence imports, and the two observed knowledge entrypoints can affect whether a required workflow provisions its import closure. Dependency lock/constraint manifests remain deliberately outside review-family selection; they are evidence for diagnosis, not an implementation surface for this recorded family.

prevention.mechanism: Recorded finding only. A correcting contribution must derive each required workflow's import closure and compare it against that workflow's provisioned requirements, failing loudly at verification time rather than at first import, before this family can advance. The precise provisioning step that omitted the dependency in the recorded instance was not established by the completed mining and must be diagnosed before this mechanism is treated as the fix.

families.title: governance-verdict-not-machine-readable
families.invariant: Every gate emits its verdict on a machine-readable channel, and prose is derived from that verdict rather than carrying it. A consumer reads the structured verdict with all prose removed, and evidence that cannot be resolved blocks rather than degrading to an advisory note.

applicability.rationale: These surfaces emit and consume gate verdicts. Where the verdict token exists only inside a human-readable banner, any consumer that decides must substring-match prose, and a banner that cannot be produced degrades silently instead of blocking.

prevention.mechanism: Recorded finding only. A correcting contribution must give each gate a structured verdict field and require consumers to read that field, prohibiting prose-token assertions as an interface, and must make unresolvable evidence a blocking outcome rather than a non-blocking note, before this family can advance.
